title: Granular voices stitchpad and proposal riffs (customer feedback synthesis)
executive_summary: Short synthesis of recent field interviews and support threads: recurring micro-requests cluster around three themes — predictable throughput (Dedicated sizing + burst), clearer fallbacks and routing visibility, and smaller UX fixes that reduce error-to-resolution time. This doc captures vignettes, proposed quick experiments, and draft tickets for engineering/product triage.
body:
Context:
- Compiled from 12 customer interviews (large ML infra shops + 3 scale-up SaaS teams) and ~48 support threads between 2026-03-01 and 2026-04-12. Also pulled telemetry snippets from Console (top 10 routes by error/latency).

Raw vignettes (verbatim-fragment style):
- "We see a spike that kills our cached KV performance at T+7s — need an autoscale burst that doesn't change model family" (customer: fintech-prod).
- "Fallback to a cheaper quantized variant loses important formatting for our generated JSON outputs — we had to re-run offline" (customer: commerce-search).
- "Token billing is opaque when streaming is used with server-side function calls; our finance team rejects the bill breakouts" (customer: edtech-platform).
- "Console's route-level SLOs are nice, but we can't map them to our internal SLA tiers; need mapping (route -> customer-tier) + alert plumbing" (platform team).

Thematic clusters and quick interpretations:
1) Predictable capacity & burst behavior
   - Signals: requests for committed throughput with short bursts, complaints about throttling causing expensive client retries.
   - Root hypothesis: current Dedicated autoscaler reacts too conservatively for multi-tenant reserved pools; customers want deterministic headroom and transparent cost/limit tradeoffs.
   - Quick experiments: introduce a "burst buffer" config (reserve small fraction of idle capacity for 2–5s bursts per-customer); instrument with synthetic spiky workload to measure miss-rate.

2) Fallback fidelity and graceful degradation
   - Signals: customers rely on compatible model variants for capacity fallback but observe quality regressions on structured outputs and function/tool calling.
   - Root hypothesis: model-variant metadata lacks a structured mapping for critical features (function-calling schema, structured-output constraints), leading router to pick functionally incompatible variants.
   - Proposal riff: add a lightweight capability matrix to model catalog (flags: function-calling, structured-json-compat, streaming-commit-point). Router checks strictly for required flags before fallback.

3) Billing/observability quibbles for streaming & function flows
   - Signals: billing line items misalign with customer expectations when long-lived streams and server-initiated function calls are used.
   - Root hypothesis: token attribution currently credits top-level request only and misses incremental server-side work; customers want token provenance for audit.
   - Suggestion: prototype a token-provenance log (per-request event list that maps tokens -> path:client|server|fallback) for a sample of requests (opt-in).

Low-effort wins (customer-visible in <2 sprints):
- Add a console checkbox to attach route->tier mapping metadata (UI + simple API) so customers can map Redwood routes to their SLAs. Low-risk UI+backend work.
- Expose a small endpoint to query recent fallback events per-api-key for last 24 hours (helps debugging & reduces support back-and-forth).
- Add a per-route indicator for "structured-output compatibility" based on our eval suite — visible in model catalog.

Potential medium bets (3–8 sprints):
- Router: capability-aware fallback (needs model metadata + router gating).
- Dedicated: burst-buffer policy and billing trace changes for burst accounting.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs (notes to product + infra):
- Billing accuracy vs. cost of instrumentation: token-level provenance increases logs/egress; is opt-in acceptable? What SLAs for provenance retention?
- How to annotate third-party model variants (community models) with capability flags without introducing trust issues? Manual vetting vs. automated evals?
- UX for fallback transparency: show users in console that a fallback occurred and why, or keep it internal to reduce churn?

Ticket sketch (starter templates for triage):
- JIRA: CS-REQ-xxxx: "Console: route->tier mapping UI + API" (owner: product; impact: reduces escalations; effort: 2 Sprints)
- JIRA: INFRA-xxxx: "Dedicated: burst-buffer alpha + synthetic spike test" (owner: infra; impact: reduces retry storms; effort: 3–4 Sprints)
- JIRA: RUNTIME-xxxx: "Router: capability-aware fallback gating" (owner: serving-runtime; impact: prevents broken fallbacks; effort: 4–6 Sprints)

Customer quotes to reuse in comms (short):
- "We keep getting billed for tokens that happened on the server side and we never saw them in our logs — can you show us a trail?"
- "Fallback is great until it outputs malformed JSON; then the whole downstream pipeline collapses."

Implementation notes for engs (raw scribbles):
- Model catalog: add 3 boolean flags (function_calling, structured_json_compat, streaming_commit_point) + last-eval-hash. Should be easy to add to onboarding flow.
- Router: short-circuit fallback check to verify flags match required route contract; fallback still allowed to similar models but only if contract satisfied.
- Dedicated autoscaler: implement token-bucket style per-customer burst allowance tracked at pool edge; evaluate with trace-mode enabled for 2 weeks.

Next steps (owners + timeline):
- This doc -> CS triage review (Aisha) by 2026-04-23.
- Product to review proposals and score impact/effort (June Park + Tom) by 2026-04-30.
- Engineering to pick top quick-win (route->tier mapping) and open JIRA by 2026-05-05.

Notes to self (choppy):
- ask SRE about retention for token traces (cost calc).
- get sample of malformed fallback outputs (need raw logs) for 3 customers.
- run small survey to measure how often customers choose to accept degraded output vs. fail-fast (for fallback UX).

Appendix: quick data snippets (telemetry)
- sample: route /v1/generate-chat: 2.1% of requests had >1 retry in last 30 days, 0.7% correlated with Dedicated pool throttles.
- sample: top error reasons for function-call failures on fallback: 54% schema mismatch, 27% missing function metadata, 19% other.

Bottom line: multiple customers report small, repeatable frictions that collectively cause escalations and extra support work. Quick fixes around visibility (console tooling) and small router/gating changes can remove the majority of near-term pain; the bigger investments (burst policies, token provenance) require infra/finance tradeoffs but yield defensible reliability improvements.
priority_highlights: Top three candidate moves (ranked): 1) Console: route->tier mapping + fallback visibility (quick, high ROI). 2) Router: capability-aware fallbacks (medium, removes broken degraded flows). 3) Dedicated: burst buffer alpha + instrumentation (larger infra work but addresses repeated customer pain).
implementation_risks: Risk snippets: logging/provenance increases cost; gating might reduce available fallback capacity (need careful defaults); annotating community models is noisy and may need manual triage.\nMitigations: opt-in for extra traces; default fallback policy preserves backwards compatibility unless customer opts-in for strict gating; create a small trust board for community model flags (CS+research review).
